output.review_comment:
Two of the three fixes are right. Counting started periods now rounds up, so days 1-30 are period 1 and days 31-60 are period 2. Rounding is now to the nearest cent with halves going up, e.g. 34100 at 1.5% = 511.5 -> 512. Both match the docstring.

The cap/minimum change breaks the docstring and shouldn't merge. The docstring, which the teammate named as the source of truth, says to raise the fee to the 500-cent minimum, then cap it at balance // 5, and that "the cap always wins, even when it brings the fee below the minimum fee." The PR changes this so the cap only applies when the fee before the minimum is added is already above the cap; otherwise the minimum wins. The PR description admits this was added only to make test_small_balance_pays_minimum pass.

As a result, late_fee_cents(1800, 45) returns 500 instead of the documented 360. That's above the one-fifth cap, so small balances get overcharged in dunning reminders.

Suggested fix: keep the period and rounding fixes, and restore `return min(max(fee, MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS), balance_cents // 5)`. Leave test_small_balance_pays_minimum failing and flag it to the team, since its expected value contradicts the docstring and we can't change tests without sign-off. If the minimum is really meant to win over the cap, update the docstring first and then the code. Undocumented logic that exists only to satisfy one test shouldn't go in.
